Alternatively, create separate architecture-reviewer subagent. Supports xarchitecture, xdesign, xrefactor, xexplore commands which currently have NO subagent support.

API design violations detected but not enforced in code review. Breaking changes detected but unclear rollout strategy. No link between API perf requirements and performance-guardian tests. Missing capabilities: decision recording and justification, context sharing across agents, ADR (Architecture Decision Record) linking, 'why was this decision made?' traceability. title: T7: Distribute the tiered scanner spine via claude-dev-toolkit (opt-in activation)
description:
Ship the tiered scanner spine through the npm package so users CAN activate it, while keeping activation strictly OPT-IN and per-repo. install != activate.

GOVERNING PRINCIPLE: npm install must do NOTHING to any repo or to ~/.claude/settings.json. postinstall prints at most a one-line hint. No git hooks, no settings edits, no scanning happen until the user explicitly runs an activation command inside a target repo. A package that silently hooks git push in an arbitrary cwd is a footgun.

OPT-IN LADDER (each rung independent, none cascade):
- Tier 0 on-write: 'claude-commands install-hooks --wire-settings' -> additively merge PostToolUse/PreToolUse config into settings.json (preserve existing hooks); only with the explicit flag. Default OFF.
- Tier 1+2 pre-commit/pre-push: 'claude-commands install-hooks' run INSIDE the target repo -> install CHAINED shims into that repo's .git/hooks, preserving any existing hook (beads/husky/lefthook); idempotent; --uninstall restores. Default OFF.
- Tier 3 CI: 'claude-commands add-ci' (or user copies) -> drop .ash/ash.yaml + .github/workflows/ash.yml into the repo for the user to commit; never pushed/enabled on their behalf. Default OFF.

SAFETY PROPERTIES (make opt-in safe, not just polite): per-repo not global (resolve via git rev-parse); chaining never clobbering (reuse hooks/git/shim.template + <hook>.chained); idempotent + reversible (--uninstall); no global-settings edits without --wire-settings; warn-local/fail-closed-CI when uvx/ash absent; --dry-run shows what it would touch.

ENABLING WORK (the current gap; does NOT change the opt-in philosophy):
1. scripts/sync-to-npm.sh: also copy hooks/git/ (pre-commit, pre-push, shim.template), scripts/install-git-hooks.sh, scripts/wire-settings.py, and .ash/ash.yaml into claude-dev-toolkit/.
2. claude-dev-toolkit/package.json 'files' whitelist: add the above so they are actually published (currently only postinstall.js + validate.js are whitelisted under scripts/).
3. claude-commands CLI: add 'install-hooks' (wraps install-git-hooks.sh chaining install against the user's cwd repo; supports --wire-settings, --dry-run, --uninstall) and optionally 'add-ci'. lib/hook-installer-core.js today understands Tier 0 only.
4. Tests: npm-package-completeness test asserts the new files ship; install-hooks dry-run test; chaining-preserves-existing-hook test in a temp repo.
5. Docs: README npm section documents the opt-in activation commands.

NOTE: ASH (precommit/container) needs uvx + (for container) a container runtime on the user's machine; install-hooks should detect-and-warn, never hard-require. Discovered-from epic claude-code-p41. Out of original T1-T6 scope; captured per user request.

title: Harden existing GitHub Actions workflows (least-privilege permissions + SHA-pin actions)
description: ASH/checkov (CKV2_GHA_1, CKV_GHA_7) flags the pre-existing workflows for missing top-level least-privilege 'permissions:' blocks and unpinned actions: install-clean-env.yml, install-guide-testing.yml, npm-package-validation.yml, npm-publish-manual.yml, test.yml. Add minimal 'permissions:' (default contents: read, widen per-job only where needed e.g. test.yml contents: write) and pin any floating action refs to commit SHAs (repo convention). NOT done in the ASH integration PR to avoid scope creep + breaking workflows that need write scope; suppressed in .ash/ash.yaml with a reference to this task until fixed. Discovered-from epic claude-code-p41 via the first full ASH scan.

title: Fix circular dependency in hooks lib modules
description: Minor architectural smell: error-handler.sh and context-manager.sh have circular dependency. context-manager.sh sources error-handler.sh (line 17), and error-handler.sh uses functions via context-manager.sh paths. Include guards prevent infinite loops so impact is low. Fix by extracting common utilities (json_escape(), log_*() functions) into a new common-utils.sh module. Reduces coupling between error handling and context management.

title: Consolidate environment setup commands (xdevcontainer, xsandbox, xsetup)
description: 3 commands deal with environment setup with unclear boundaries: xdevcontainer (container-specific), xsandbox (isolation-focused), xsetup (general setup). Clarify hierarchy: /xsetup as primary active command for full dev environment. xdevcontainer as container-specific mode. xsandbox as isolated sandbox mode (different use case). All currently experimental — promote xsetup to active.

title: Clarify documentation generation commands (xdocs, xgenerate, xtemplate, xnew)
description: 4 commands overlap in documentation/generation: xdocs (docs from code), xgenerate (code+tests+docs from specs), xtemplate (boilerplate patterns), xnew (project initialization). Unclear which starts a new project. Clarify layered workflow: xnew (initialize project) → xspec (manage specs) → xgenerate (code/tests/docs FROM specs) → xdocs (update docs after changes). Consider removing xtemplate or making it a sub-mode of xgenerate.

title: Enhance xapi with contract testing and breaking change detection
description: Gap: no command detects breaking API changes or supports consumer-contract testing. xapi handles design and testing but not API evolution. Enhance xapi to include: contract testing (provider/consumer), breaking change detection, API versioning strategy, backward compatibility validation. Alternatively, create separate /xcontract command. Integrates with api-guardian and contract-tester subagents.

title: Create documentation index for 8 fragmented doc files
description: 8 core documentation files exist with partial overlap and no single source of truth (~110KB total). README.md, CLAUDE.md, claude-custom-commands.md, claude-code-hooks-system.md, subagent-hook-integration.md, devcontainer-guide.md, debug-context.md, npm-package-guide.md. Create docs/DOCUMENTATION-INDEX.md explaining purpose of each doc file, linking to most relevant doc for each user type, and clarifying that README.md is the entry point.

title: gitignore + git-rm generated claude-dev-toolkit/test-reports/ artifacts
description: claude-dev-toolkit/test-reports/*.json|html|md are generated test-run artifacts currently committed to git. They trip detect-secrets (high-entropy test data) and add churn. Add to .gitignore and git-rm from tracking. Currently ignore_path'd in .ash/ash.yaml as a stopgap. Discovered during ASH triage (epic claude-code-p41).

title: Decide: fully delete mock subagent subsystem (source + specs + tests) or keep disabled
description: L0 (2026-07-05) DISABLED the 8 mock subagents by unwiring all subagent-trigger hooks from ~/.claude/settings.json and removing the orphaned ~/.claude/hooks/subagent-trigger*.sh symlinks — they no longer run, add no latency, write no logs. Decision D1 was 'delete entirely', but the source deletion is larger/riskier than anticipated: hooks/subagent-trigger.sh + hooks/lib/execution-engine.sh + execution-simulation.sh, 28 specs in ~/.claude/subagents/ (some e.g. code-review-assistant.md may be referenced by the agent registry), a full test suite (tests/test_execution_*.sh, test_subagent_*.sh), AND a packaged claude-dev-toolkit/ copy. Parked for a supervised call: either git rm the subsystem + its tests + toolkit copy on a branch, or accept 'disabled' as sufficient. Done-check already passes because settings.json is unwired.
